headline: The Agent Platform — role-based chat agents, custom agent personas, admin and manager screens, an in-app help assistant, and agent security monitoring — is largely backed by code, with 8 of 10 tickets supported, 2 not settled, and 1 backlog item that appears already built.
what_is_there: The code shows a catalogue of agent personas with role-specific base prompts plus user-added instructions, admin and user-facing screens for creating, editing and deleting agents, a floating in-app help assistant, security checks that block risky agent actions and email an administrator when they fire, and a bundled library of reusable skills seeded at startup into an editable skill manager.
what_is_unclear: Two items could not be confirmed from the code that was examined: a general tool registry classifying tools as read, write or execute (only one connector family showed a read/write split), and a human approval step for command execution (automated security blocking was found, but no approve-or-deny prompt or pending-request queue). Some supporting documentation referenced during the review described a different codebase, so it carried no weight.
suggested_action: Ask the team where the tool scope registry and the human command-approval step live, and confirm whether the skill-standardisation item still open in the tracker should be closed given the skill library already present.
caveat: Several reference documents cited in the analysis describe a different repository and name files that do not exist here, so any conclusions resting on them should be discounted.
